name: Alcalde
description: Alcalde is a unique three-player trick-taking game from Puerto Rico. It is an asymmetrical variant of Brisca where one player, the 'Alcalde' (Mayor), defends their position against two cooperating opponents. The Alcalde wields twice the cards and twice the play-power in every trick.

overview.description: Alcalde is a unique three-player trick-taking game from Puerto Rico. It is an asymmetrical variant of Brisca where one player, the 'Alcalde' (Mayor), defends their position against two cooperating opponents. The Alcalde wields twice the cards and twice the play-power in every trick.

history.origins: Rooted in the Spanish Brisca tradition, Alcalde evolved in Puerto Rico as a social game where the leader is challenged by a temporary alliance. Its name, 'Alcalde', reflects the local governance structure where the 'Mayor' must satisfy the points to retain their office.
timeline: 1800s: Brisca becomes the dominant trick-taking game in Puerto Rico.
Early 1900s: Asymmetrical variants for odd player counts (3 or 5) emerge.
1990s: Formal rules documented by José M. Carrillo-Muniz.
history.cultural: Commonly played in plazas and community centers in Puerto Rico. The 'Alcalde' role is often rotated, symbolizing the fleeting nature of political power.
history.evolution: Transitioned from a 4-player partnership game to a '1 vs 2' format where the single player is compensated with larger hand size and draw priority.

setup.deck: 40-card Spanish pack. Rank: Ace-3-King-Queen-Jack-7-6-5-4-2 (in order of power/value).
setup.dealing: Alcalde deals 3 cards to each opponent and 6 cards to themselves. The next card is the 'Life' card (Trump indicator).

rules.objective: As Alcalde: Score 60+ points to retain the title. As Opponents: Prevent the Alcalde from reaching 60 points to depose them.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trump Exchange**: Any player with the 7 or 2 of trumps can swap it for the face-up 'Life' card if the Life card is a point card (A, 3, K, Q, J). 2. **Cooperation**: The two opponents may peek at each other's hands throughout the game but are forbidden from verbal signaling. 3. **The Trick**: Play is counter-clockwise. Each opponent plays ONE card. The Alcalde then plays TWO cards. 4. **No Follow Suit**: Players can play any card; they are not required to follow the suit of the lead. 5. **Winning Tricks**: The highest trump wins. If no trumps, the highest card of the led suit wins. 6. **Drawing**: After a trick, the winner draws (2 cards for Alcalde, 1 for opponents) followed by others in order.
keyRules: Alcalde plays twice per trick, meaning they control the final 'slap' of the round.
Point Values: Ace=11, 3=10, King=4, Queen=3, Jack=2. Total in deck = 120 points.
The 'Life' card is drawn as the very last card of the deck.
If the Alcalde fails to reach 60, the player to their right becomes the new Alcalde for the next hand.

strategy.basic: As Alcalde, you have a 6-card hand. Use your first card of the trick to 'tease' and your second card to 'win' the point cards played by opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Opponents must coordinate their discards. If one opponent 'feeds' a point card to the trick, the other should play a trump if they suspect the Alcalde will scoop it.
strategy.advanced: Exchange management: If you have the 7 of trumps, wait until the Life card (e.g., an Ace) is about to be drawn or until you need it to win a critical 60-point trick.
tips: The 3 (worth 10 points) is often more dangerous than the Ace because it is harder to see coming.
As Alcalde, try to drain the opponents of trumps early so your point cards become safe 'good' leads.

variations.name: Fixed Alcalde
variations.description: The same player remains Alcalde for a set number of hands regardless of score.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Fixed Alcalde is documented as a scoring and role-rotation variant; engine overrides are not modeled yet.

scoring.description: Scoring is determined by the total 120 card points captured in tricks.
scoring.winCondition: Alcalde needs 60 points to 'win'. If they hit 60+, they score 1 game point and stay in office. If <60, opponents each score 1 game point.

sources.name: Jose Carrillo - Games with the Spanish Pack (Alcalde)

synthesis.shortDescription: Step into the plazas of Puerto Rico. In this high-tension 1-vs-2 challenge, the Alcalde holds the cards, but the people hold the points. Can you reach 60?

hero.title: ALCALDE
hero.subtitle: The Mayor's Gambit
hero.tagline: Two hands against one. Do you have the votes to stay in power?
